input.rationale: Recorded the executed control receipt in the question account: the same crash pattern with the recovery driven by the replica that holds the value preserves it (comparisons hold), so the loss is tied to a coordinator that lacks the command. The question's own discrimination is answered, so its disposition is set to explained, and an independent sourced question is opened on the recovery ballot/authority path that the same code gates on IsLeader.

investigations.question: Can a recovering replica that is not the master-designated leader recover an instance whose accepted value sits at a ballot above its own recovery ballot, or does the periodic retry repeat the same rejected prepare with no enabled repair?
investigations.hypothesis: makeBallot gives a fixed ballot per replica (r.Id for the instance owner, r.Id+N otherwise) and climbs above maxRecvBallot only while r.IsLeader is true; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the master's BeTheLeader RPC sets it, so for every other replica a prepare at its fixed ballot is rejected by any acceptor whose stored bal is higher, and the three nack repairs (handlePreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply, handlePrepareReply) are all gated on r.IsLeader. executeCommands re-enqueues the same instance every COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, so the same rejected prepare is repeated without a ballot advance, and instances that depend on the stuck instance cannot execute.
investigations.discriminator: Whether two consecutive startRecoveryForInstance calls on a non-designated replica emit the identical Prepare ballot while the acceptors' replies all report a higher stored ballot, with no higher-ballot Prepare emitted and the instance uncommitted; and whether the same call on a replica with IsLeader true emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: in the executed scenario the captured EPaxos package loses an accepted value during recovery of the instance by a replica that does not itself hold the command, and decides a different value for that instance. Witnesses from receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryValueAdoption, 24 parsed events, no parsing errors): event 5 shows leader 0 in status ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 after the non-equal pre-accept phase; event 6 shows the Accept broadcast to replicas 2 and 3 at ballot 0; event 7 shows replica 2 carrying the PUT (cmd_op 1) at vbal 0 after the Accept, event 8 shows replica 3 holding the same coordinates with no command (has_cmds false, status NONE) and vbal 0, and event 9 shows leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 immediately before it fails. The instance (0,0) value was therefore accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3, i.e. by a quorum of the five replicas, and no replica had committed it when leader 0 failed after the Accept broadcast. Event 11 records the recovery start by replica 3: tried_ballot 8 and its own self reply carrying self_vballot 8 with self_status NONE and self_has_command false, while startRecoveryForInstance had set lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145) and had overwritten inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1150-1153, anchor s-decl-recovery). Events 12 and 13 show the Prepare broadcast at ballot 8; event 14 shows replica 2's PrepareReply carrying the PUT at vballot 0 (status PREACCEPTED_EQ) with Ballot 8 after joining, and event 15 the reply of replica 4 with no command; event 16 states the decisive operands: self_vballot 8, max_remote_vballot_with_command 0, so the self ballot is above every remote value ballot, and quorum_reply_command_op 1. Comparison 0 is violated with complete witness 17: the PreAccept the recovery emitted (ballot 8, cmd_len 1) carries cmd_op 0, i.e. state.NOOP(), while quorum_reply_command_op is 1 - the adoption loop at epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 (anchor s-decl-prepare-reply) keeps lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE because the self reply is evaluated first with the fabricated vbal 8 and the genuine reply at vbal 0 fails the >= test, so sub-case 6 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1278-1279) calls startPhase1 with the NOOP (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1313). Events 18-21 show the consequence: the recovered NOOP became the instance's value at replicas 2, 3 and 4 (status 4 COMMITTED, cmd_op 0), the quiescent run completed, and comparison 1 is violated with complete witness 20: replica 2, which held the accepted PUT after the Accept phase (event 7), ended holding the NOOP (cmd_op 0), i.e. the recovery overwrote the only live copy of the accepted command. Events 22 and 23 record the failed replicas' retained state: replica 1 still PREACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 and leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1, so the recovered decision (NOOP at ballot 8) is a different value for instance (0,0) than the value those replicas accepted at ballot 0. This establishes the scoped defect: after a permitted leader failure in the accept window, a recovery driven by a replica that knows the instance without its command proposes and commits a NOOP instead of the value the prepare replies carry, discarding a quorum-accepted value rather than completing it.

aa497fcd14934325ba2eabe45fefecd1-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by the executed scenario: with replica 1 failing after replying to the PreAccept but before the Accept broadcast, the target's own handleAccept left replica 3 with instance (0,0) known to its executor (crtInstance[0] advanced) while holding no command - event 8 (has_cmds false, status NONE, bal and vbal 0) and event 10 - and replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance then let the fabricated self reply (event 11: self_vballot 8, status NONE, no command) decide the adopted value, producing the NOOP proposal of event 17 and the committed NOOP of events 19-21. The accept-broadcast peer set differing from the pre-accept peer set is thus sufficient and was realised under the harness's crash model (reply delivered, then the peer marked failed before the broadcast).

counterevidence: The defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the command, and this bound is now executed, not merely sourced: the control experiment 242eaa8afa384a87b0952fbcd4b074b4-experiment (receipt 9d07449105684a498113db891da025d9, exit 0) replayed the identical crash pattern with the recovery driven by replica 2, which holds X at value ballot 0; its declared preservation comparisons both hold, evaluating parsed index 17 (the recovered PreAccept carries cmd_op 1 although no remote reply carries a command) and indices 19-20 (replica 2 remains at cmd_op 1 through quiescence). The value-adoption receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 is the same harness with only the recoverer changed to replica 3, which holds no command, so the loss is tied to the coordinator's missing value rather than to the crash pattern.

Event 16 also shows the comparison is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted, so a higher-id replica's later recovery at a higher ballot is not excluded by this mechanism.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in this execution and in epaxos.New; the designated leader's climbing behaviour (epaxos/epaxos.go:1121-1125, master-driven) was excluded from the scope, so nothing here claims that a designated leader could not recover.

The executed value X was accepted by a quorum but never COMMITTED at any replica before the leader failed (no Commit message appears in the event stream); the witness therefore contradicts a quorum-accepted (chosen) value, not a value whose commit notification had been delivered.
limitations: One configuration and one instance: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), a single PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP generated by the recovery; the harness's event stream is the target's own messages and handler state, but no other command shape, key or instance index was exercised.

The harness schedules delivery explicitly instead of waiting for timers: the startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) call is the function the executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417), but the call itself was made by the harness, and no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine was active; the same holds for the control receipt 9d07449105684a498113db891da025d9.

The premise that the accept broadcast reaches a replica that never pre-accepted was produced by setting the failed peer's Alive flag false between the pre-accept and accept broadcasts (the peer's reply was delivered, then it was marked failed), matching the target's own Alive mechanism for choosing recipients; a real connection loss was not exercised.

Incidental observation not used by the claim: the committed recovered instance ends with Seq -1 at replicas 2, 3 and 4 (events 19-21) although startPhase1 computed seq 0 (event 18); this ordering field is recorded here as a separate lead, not as support for the adoption claim.
interpretations.joint_history: Producer events 12-15 (Prepare/PrepareReply traffic between replicas 3, 2 and 4) and result events 17-21 all belong to receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 for fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment; events 7-9 are the same run's pre-recovery state of the same instance (0,0).

investigations.question: When a replica that does not itself hold the value recovers instance (replica A, instance i), does the recovery adopt the value that prepare replies report as accepted/pre-accepted, or does it replace that value with a NOOP?
investigations.hypothesis: startRecoveryForInstance sets inst.vbal to the newly tried ballot and puts its own PrepareReply (VBallot = that ballot, Status/Command from its own possibly empty local state) first into lb.prepareReplies; the adoption loop only takes replies with VBallot >= the running candidate ballot, so genuine replies at the real value ballot are skipped and the recovery proceeds to sub-case 6 with a NOOP command.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a permitted execution can reach recovery at a replica whose crtInstance[A] >= i while its own instance holds no command (no pre-accept, e.g. it only received an Accept because the pre-accept peer set and accept peer set differed); and whether the emitted PreAccept after recovery carries Command NOOP while a delivered prepare reply carried the accepted command at a lower vbal.

gaps.question: Does a permitted execution produce a recovery coordinator that knows instance (A, i) (crtInstance[A] >= i) but holds no command for it, so that the fabricated self-reply decides the adopted value? Candidate: an Accept-phase broadcast to a different peer set than the PreAccept broadcast (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts at the leader) lets a replica learn the instance with Status NONE and Cmds nil.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the recovery path in the captured EPaxos package can replace a quorum-held value with a NOOP, contrary to its own stated case analysis. Basis is source-level: (1) epaxos/epaxos.go:1145 sets lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal, then :1150-1153 call makeBallot and overwrite inst.vbal with lb.lastTriedBallot, and :1154-1165 append a self PrepareReply carrying that new ballot as VBallot together with inst.Status/inst.Cmds (NONE/nil for a replica that never pre-accepted, e.g. one whose only knowledge of the instance is an Accept, epaxos/epaxos.go:995-1005, which stores Deps/Seq/bal/vbal but neither Cmds nor a status). (2) epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 adopts values only when reply.VBallot >= the running candidate and processes the self-reply first, so a genuine remote reply whose VBallot is the real value ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1191-1201 reports inst.vbal unchanged by the prepare) is skipped once the fabricated self-ballot is larger. (3) With lb.status still NONE, :1278-1279 selects sub-case 6 and :1307-1313 calls startPhase1 with state.NOOP() because lb.cmds is nil, i.e. the recovery proposes a different value for the instance even though the reply set carried the accepted/pre-accepted one. The code's own comment at :1228-1235 states that these sub-cases (including '2 -> accepted' and '3 -> pre-accepted ... and allEqual') are meant to take replies' values into account, so the fabricated self-ballot defeats the documented case analysis for any coordinator that lacks the value itself. Scope of the claim: the recovery proposes NOOP instead of the quorum-held value; whether the NOOP then reaches a majority and erases the accepted value at every live replica (and thus produces two different decisions for instance (A, i) versus the crashed leader's state) is the next discriminator, not asserted here. Limits: not executed; the reachability premise (a coordinator knowing the instance without holding the command) is registered as a necessary gap; the ballot comparison also means a genuine reply with a value ballot above the coordinator's own recovery ballot is still adopted, and recovery by the replica that itself pre-accepted the value does adopt it (its self-reply carries the real Status/Cmds), so the defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the value.
counterevidence: epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451: makeBallot climbs above maxRecvBallot when IsLeader is true, so the master-designated leader (epaxos/epaxos.go:1121-1125) gets a ballot above existing ones; that does not remove the fabrication (the self-reply is still the top ballot in its own reply set), but a designated leader's recovery is what keeps the ballot from being permanently rejected, so it must not be confused with the adoption defect.

epaxos/epaxos.go:1255-1303: when the recovering replica itself holds the pre-accepted value (thrifty keeps the accept peer set a subset of the pre-accept peer set, epaxos/epaxos.go:510-513 and 571-586), the self-reply carries that value and sub-cases 1-3 can still complete the instance; the value loss is therefore not universal to all recoveries.
limitations: No execution receipt: the account rests on source reading of the captured snapshot (fixed revision), not on a completed witness.

The scenario in which the recovering replica knows the instance without its command is sourced but not yet demonstrated; it requires the accept-phase peer set to differ from the pre-accept peer set (peer liveness change between the two broadcasts) or an equivalent observer.

materials.text:
inst.lb = r.newLeaderBookkeepingDefault()
	lb := inst.lb
	lb.clientProposals = proposals
	lb.ballot = inst.vbal
	lb.seq = inst.Seq
	lb.cmds = inst.Cmds
	lb.deps = inst.Deps
	lb.status = inst.Status
	r.makeBallot(replica, instance)

	inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	preply := &PrepareReply{
		r.Id,
		replica,
		instance,
		inst.bal,
		inst.vbal,
		inst.Status,
		inst.Cmds,
		inst.Seq,
		inst.Deps}

	lb.prepareReplies = append(lb.prepareReplies, preply)
	lb.leaderResponded = r.Id == replica

	r.bcastPrepare(replica, instance)

Witnesses from receipt 143e14592eea4c42b3c81044e3860348 (fixed experiment fc825b4d2a9c488e8c03dff32b05cab7-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryValueAdoption, 24 parsed events, no parsing errors): event 5 shows leader 0 in status ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 after the non-equal pre-accept phase; event 6 shows the Accept broadcast to replicas 2 and 3 at ballot 0; event 7 shows replica 2 carrying the PUT (cmd_op 1) at vbal 0 after the Accept, event 8 shows replica 3 holding the same coordinates with no command (has_cmds false, status NONE) and vbal 0, and event 9 shows leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 immediately before it fails. The instance (0,0) value was therefore accepted at ballot 0 by replicas 0, 2 and 3, i.e. by a quorum of the five replicas, and no replica had committed it when leader 0 failed after the Accept broadcast. Event 11 records the recovery start by replica 3: tried_ballot 8 and its own self reply carrying self_vballot 8 with self_status NONE and self_has_command false, while startRecoveryForInstance had set lb.ballot to the pre-recovery local vbal (epaxos/epaxos.go:1145) and had overwritten inst.vbal with the freshly tried ballot (epaxos/epaxos.go:1150-1153, anchor s-decl-recovery). Events 12 and 13 show the Prepare broadcast at ballot 8; event 14 shows replica 2's PrepareReply carrying the PUT at vballot 0 (status PREACCEPTED_EQ) with Ballot 8 after joining, and event 15 the reply of replica 4 with no command; event 16 states the decisive operands: self_vballot 8, max_remote_vballot_with_command 0, so the self ballot is above every remote value ballot, and quorum_reply_command_op 1. Comparison 0 is violated with complete witness 17: the PreAccept the recovery emitted (ballot 8, cmd_len 1) carries cmd_op 0, i.e. state.NOOP(), while quorum_reply_command_op is 1 - the adoption loop at epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 (anchor s-decl-prepare-reply) keeps lb.cmds nil and lb.status NONE because the self reply is evaluated first with the fabricated vbal 8 and the genuine reply at vbal 0 fails the >= test, so sub-case 6 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1278-1279) calls startPhase1 with the NOOP (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1313). Events 18-21 show the consequence: the recovered NOOP became the instance's value at replicas 2, 3 and 4 (status 4 COMMITTED, cmd_op 0), the quiescent run completed, and comparison 1 is violated with complete witness 20: replica 2, which held the accepted PUT after the Accept phase (event 7), ended holding the NOOP (cmd_op 0), i.e. the recovery overwrote the only live copy of the accepted command. Events 22 and 23 record the failed replicas' retained state: replica 1 still PREACCEPTED with cmd_op 1 and leader 0 still ACCEPTED with cmd_op 1, so the recovered decision (NOOP at ballot 8) is a different value for instance (0,0) than the value those replicas accepted at ballot 0. This establishes the scoped defect: after a permitted leader failure in the accept window, a recovery driven by a replica that knows the instance without its command proposes and commits a NOOP instead of the value the prepare replies carry, discarding a quorum-accepted value rather than completing it.

aa497fcd14934325ba2eabe45fefecd1-gap-0.explanation: Resolved by the executed scenario: with replica 1 failing after replying to the PreAccept but before the Accept broadcast, the target's own handleAccept left replica 3 with instance (0,0) known to its executor (crtInstance[0] advanced) while holding no command - event 8 (has_cmds false, status NONE, bal and vbal 0) and event 10 - and replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance then let the fabricated self reply (event 11: self_vballot 8, status NONE, no command) decide the adopted value, producing the NOOP proposal of event 17 and the committed NOOP of events 19-21. The accept-broadcast peer set differing from the pre-accept peer set is thus sufficient and was realised under the harness's crash model (reply delivered, then the peer marked failed before the broadcast).

counterevidence: The defect is bounded to coordinators that lack the command: when the recovering replica itself pre-accepted the value (thrifty makes the accept peer set a subset of the pre-accept peer set, epaxos/epaxos.go:510-513 and 571-586), its self reply carries the real Status and Cmds, the fabricated vbal 8 is self-consistent with that value, and sub-cases 3-5 can re-propose it. This path is sourced (epaxos/epaxos.go:1255-1313) but was not part of this execution, so the executed witness must not be read as claiming that every recovery loses the value.

Event 16 also shows the comparison is a ballot ordering, not a general discard: a reply whose value ballot exceeded the coordinator's own recovery ballot would still be adopted, so a higher-id replica's later recovery at a higher ballot is not excluded by this mechanism.

The countervailing ballot-climb path in makeBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451) is gated on IsLeader, which is false in this execution and in epaxos.New; the designated leader's climbing behaviour (epaxos/epaxos.go:1121-1125, master-driven) was excluded from the scope, so nothing here claims that a designated leader could not recover.

The executed value X was accepted by a quorum but never COMMITTED at any replica before the leader failed (no Commit message appears in the event stream); the witness therefore contradicts a quorum-accepted (chosen) value, not a value whose commit notification had been delivered.
limitations: One configuration and one instance: N=5, F=2, instance (0,0), a single PUT command (key 1) and the NOOP generated by the recovery; the harness's event stream is the target's own messages and handler state, but no other command shape, key or instance index was exercised.

The harness schedules delivery explicitly instead of waiting for timers: replica 3's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) call is the function the executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417), but the call itself was made by the harness, and no run() loop or executeCommands goroutine was active.

The premise that the accept broadcast reaches a replica that never pre-accepted was produced by setting the failed peer's Alive flag false between the pre-accept and accept broadcasts (the peer's reply was delivered, then it was marked failed), matching the target's own Alive mechanism for choosing recipients; a real connection loss was not exercised.

Incidental observation not used by the claim: the committed recovered instance ends with Seq -1 at replicas 2, 3 and 4 (events 19-21) although startPhase1 computed seq 0 (event 18); this ordering field is recorded here as a separate lead, not as support for the adoption claim.
